title: Stratification of a sheaf on a relative line
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $\mathbf A^1_{Y_0}$ [def-sbc-affine-space], with Weil sheaf understood in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] and lisse in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. There are finite stratifications of source and target by locally closed reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], compatible with the projection, such that $\mathcal F$ restricts to a lisse Weil sheaf on every source stratum and each induced map to its target stratum is either separated quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] or smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with one-dimensional affine geometric fibres. All strata and their immersions are defined over $k_0$.

proof.text: Every scheme here is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the field $k_0$, whose only ideals are $0$ and $k_0$. We use closed-subset induction, justified by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. The inductive assertion for a closed subset $T\subseteq Y_0$ is the claimed pair of finite stratifications over its reduced closed subscheme $T_0$, for every restricted constructible Weil sheaf. The empty subset has the empty partitions. Restrictions to the reduced locally closed schemes below remain constructible Weil sheaves: [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category] specifies inverse image on the existing constructible Weil heart for every finite-type $k_0$-morphism. We only restrict the sheaf; we do not assert a coefficient-category equivalence with the reduction.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1, reduced strata and Noetherian induction

proof.text: We will also need a finite lissity partition on any reduced separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $W_0$ carrying a constructible Weil sheaf $G$. Apply [lem-zl-weil-generic-lissity] to obtain a dense open $O_0$ on which $G$ is lisse. Apply the same assertion inductively to the reduced closed complement. The empty case and closed-subset induction give finitely many locally closed reduced pieces, all over $k_0$, with lisse restrictions. If affine pieces are needed, apply [lem-zl-affine-partition] separately to these finitely many Noetherian pieces. Restrictions of lisse adic sheaves to those reduced immersions are lisse: pull back their etale local trivializations at each finite coefficient level; the same tensor-transition isomorphisms remain isomorphisms after pullback, and rationalization and coefficient extension preserve these trivializations. The Frobenius isomorphism restricts along every $k_0$-immersion.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, choose a finite lissity stratification of the boundary

proof.text: For a nonempty reduced $T_0$, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finitely many irreducible components $C_a$. Each contains a nonempty open of $T_0$ by [lem-sfb-noetherian-component-open]. Remove the other components from that open; the result still contains the generic point of $C_a$. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $A_a=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ of that point inside it, using the affine-open basis of a scheme. The $A_a$ are disjoint, and are integral because they are reduced and lie in one irreducible component. Their union is dense in $T_0$. It suffices to construct the strata over a smaller nonempty open $V_a\subseteq A_a$ for each $a$; their union will still contain every generic point.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, disjoint integral affine opens

proof.text: Fix $A=\operatorname{Spec}B$ among these integral affine opens. Its relative line is $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$ by [def-sbc-affine-space], and is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. Apply [lem-zl-weil-generic-lissity] to the restricted sheaf on this reduced separated finite-type scheme, obtaining a nonempty open $U_0\subseteq\mathbf A^1_A$, defined over $k_0$, with lisse restriction. Let $Z_0$ be the reduced closed complement, with ideal $I\subseteq B[t]$. If $Z_0$ is empty, put $V=A$; otherwise its being proper in the spectrum of the domain implies $I\ne0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1, leading coefficient and monic relation

proof.text: Let $U_V=\mathbf A^1_V\setminus Z_V$. It carries a lisse restriction, since it is an open in $U_0$. The projection $\mathbf A^1_V\to V$ is smooth of relative dimension one by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and its restriction to $U_V$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. For a geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, the boundary is a finite closed subscheme of $\mathbf A^1_{\kappa(\bar v)}$: the monic relation remains monic in every fibre. Its support is a finite set $\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}$. Thus the complementary geometric fibre is $D(\prod_i(t-a_i))$, with the empty product $1$ if $r=0$. It is affine and nonempty, and its local rings are the same as those of the affine line, so it has pure dimension one. This proves the smooth-fibre clause over $V$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, smooth open and punctured affine-line fibres

proof.text: Apply step 2 to $Z_V$, obtaining a finite partition into reduced affine strata $S_b$ on which the sheaf is lisse. By [pqf-lem-finite-qf], the finite morphism $Z_V\to V$ is quasi-finite, and [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] gives finite fibres. Each immersion $S_b\to Z_V$ is injective on the points of each fibre; hence $S_b\to V$ has finite fibres. Both $S_b$ and $V$ are affine of finite type over $k_0$; generators of the coordinate ring of $S_b$ over $k_0$ also generate it as an algebra over the coordinate ring of $V$. Thus $S_b\to V$ is finite type and quasi-compact. Apply [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] again to conclude quasi-finiteness. It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], since $S_b$ is affine. Together with $U_V$ these pieces partition the relative line over $V$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, boundary strata are separated quasi-finite

proof.text: Perform steps 4-7 on the finitely many $A_a$ and let $V=\coprod_aV_a$ be their union in $T_0$. This is an open containing every generic point; its complement $T'_0$ is a proper reduced closed subscheme of $T_0$. The induction hypothesis gives finite source and target stratifications over $T'_0$. Add the finitely many target pieces $V_a$ and their source pieces from steps 6-7. Every point of $T_0$ lies either in one $V_a$ or in $T'_0$, so the target pieces partition $T_0$, and the corresponding inverse-image source pieces partition $\mathbf A^1_{T_0}$. All are locally closed reduced subschemes, their sheaf restrictions are lisse, and each induced map has the type proved above. Closed-subset induction, including its empty case, proves finiteness and the assertion over $(Y_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Compose these reduced source and target immersions with the reduction immersions into $\mathbf A^1_{Y_0}$ and $Y_0$; they still give the required locally closed partitions, since reduction does not change the points. No assertion that $\mathcal F$ itself descends to the reduced scheme is used.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, reassembly and reduced strata

proof.text: Every scheme, polynomial, open, complement and immersion used in this construction is defined over $k_0$. In step 4 this is the finite-field-model conclusion of [lem-zl-weil-generic-lissity], and the same conclusion applies at each use in step 2. Geometric Frobenius on a base change commutes with every such immersion. Hence restricting the given isomorphism $\Phi^*\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F$ gives a Weil isomorphism on each source stratum. This verifies lissity as Weil sheaves and the claimed model compatibility without assuming that a Weil sheaf descends as an arithmetic etale sheaf, or that a chosen lattice is Frobenius-stable.

split_report.summary: Corrected the finite-coefficient convention reference to the constructible Qlbar Weil heart and adic lissity, with explicit finite-field datum and reduced model strata. Extracted only generic Weil lissity over its model; proved the leading-coefficient finiteness calculation inline, used the actual finite-fibre theorem for quasi-finiteness and the actual affine-space smoothness theorem, and made both induction arguments explicit. The existing pure-weight Lean stratification is not an attachment for arbitrary constructible sheaves.
